paragraphs: Rimmon (II Samuel 4:2). Seder HaDorot cites this name from the beginning of Midrash Shmuel, chapter 13. Hyman says a blurred copy of the midrash must have come into its author's hands, since our midrashim read Rabbi Simon.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The blurred-copy explanation belongs to Hyman. His identification of the current reading as Rabbi Simon is preserved without a new scan or manuscript claim.

The consulted Midrash Shmuel 13:1 text names Rabbi Simon. II Samuel 4:2 contains the biblical Rimmon name. These are distinct occurrences; the biblical name does not establish a sage named Rimon. Hyman’s blurred-copy explanation remains a conjecture. The abbreviated title in his heading is retained as R’.
